answer:
For one length-$d$ row, set $\mu=\operatorname{mean}(x)$, $r=(\operatorname{mean}((x-\mu)^2)+\epsilon)^{-1/2}$, $\hat x=(x-\mu)r$, and $u=g\odot\gamma$, where $g$ is the upstream gradient of $y=\gamma\odot\hat x+ eta$. Differentiating both the mean and variance gives $
abla_xL=r[u-\operatorname{mean}(u)-\hat x\operatorname{mean}(u\hat x)]$. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.07467) [2](https://www.deeplearningbook.org/)

For RMSNorm, omit centering: $r=(\operatorname{mean}(x^2)+\epsilon)^{-1/2}$ and $
abla_xL=ru-xr^3\operatorname{mean}(ux)$. Affine gradients are $
abla_\gamma L=g\odot\hat x$ and, for LayerNorm, $
abla_ eta L=g$, summed over rows sharing parameters. These formulas keep epsilon inside the normalization and use population variance. Verify analytical gradients against autograd, including constant rows and mixed precision; confusing normalized dimensions with batch dimensions produces a different operation.
